title: Frontend Developer
overview: Builds the part of a web product that people see and touch: layouts, interactions, forms and animations running in the browser.
responsibilities: Turn designs into responsive, accessible interfaces
Connect screens to backend APIs
Keep pages fast and consistent across browsers and devices
Work with designers and backend developers on how features behave
skills: A UI framework such as React
projects: A portfolio site that works on a phone
A to-do or notes app that saves to the browser
Re-create a page of a site you like with your own code

title: Backend Developer
overview: Builds the servers, APIs and databases that sit behind an application and make its features work reliably.
responsibilities: Design and implement APIs
Model and query databases
Handle authentication, validation and error cases
Monitor and improve performance and reliability
skills: A server-side language (Java, Python, Go, Node.js and others)
entryRoutes: Projects with a real database and API
projects: A REST API for a library or expense tracker
A URL shortener with a database
Add login and permissions to an existing API

title: Full-Stack Developer
overview: Works across the whole web application, from the interface to the server and database, and can take a feature from idea to working product.
responsibilities: Build user-facing features and the APIs behind them
Choose how data is stored and moved
Deploy and maintain the application
Make trade-offs between speed of delivery and quality
entryRoutes: Complete projects you can demo end to end
projects: A small marketplace or booking app with login
A chat app with a database
A dashboard fed by your own API

title: Mobile App Developer
overview: Creates apps for phones and tablets, working within device limits such as screen size, battery, connectivity and platform guidelines.
responsibilities: Build screens and navigation for Android and/or iOS
Handle offline use, notifications and device features
Publish and update apps through app stores
Test across devices and OS versions
skills: Kotlin or Swift, or a cross-platform framework
entryRoutes: Publish a small app of your own
projects: A habit tracker that works offline
A weather app using a public API
A campus events app

title: Data Analyst
overview: Answers business questions with data: cleans it, analyses it, and explains the result clearly to people who make decisions.
responsibilities: Query and clean data
Build reports and dashboards
Explain findings to non-technical colleagues
Check whether a number can be trusted
entryRoutes: College club or fest data work
projects: Analyse a public dataset and write up what you found
Build a dashboard for your own spending
Clean a messy CSV and document each decision

title: Data Scientist
overview: Uses statistics and machine learning to explore data, build predictive models and test whether they hold up.
responsibilities: Frame a question as a statistical or modelling problem
Explore and prepare data
Train and evaluate models
Communicate uncertainty and limitations honestly
projects: Predict something from a public dataset and compare against a simple baseline
A/B test analysis on simulated data
Reproduce the result of a published tutorial and extend it

title: Data Engineer
overview: Builds the pipelines and storage that move data from where it is produced to where analysts and models can use it.
responsibilities: Design and run data pipelines
Model warehouses and lakes
Keep data accurate, fresh and documented
Scale processing as data grows
projects: An ETL pipeline that loads a public API into a database every day
A small warehouse schema with sample queries
Add data-quality checks to an existing pipeline

title: ML Engineer
overview: Takes machine-learning models from experiment to something that runs reliably in a product, including training, serving and monitoring.
responsibilities: Train and tune models
Build training and inference pipelines
Deploy and monitor models in production
Track data and model versions
skills: Maths behind ML (linear algebra, probability, optimisation)
projects: Train an image classifier and serve it behind an API
Build a recommender for a small dataset
Add monitoring to a deployed model

title: AI Engineer (LLM apps)
overview: Builds applications on top of existing large language models and other AI services, such as assistants, search over documents and workflow automation.
responsibilities: Design prompts and retrieval pipelines
Integrate model APIs into products
Evaluate output quality and failure modes
Handle cost, latency, safety and privacy concerns
entryRoutes: Product or backend internships with AI features
projects: A question-answering app over your own notes
A tool that summarises and tags documents, with a written evaluation of where it fails
A chatbot with a clear 'I don't know' behaviour

title: Security Analyst
overview: Watches over an organisation's systems, investigates suspicious activity and helps reduce the chance and impact of attacks.
responsibilities: Monitor logs and alerts
Investigate and triage incidents
Track vulnerabilities and follow up on fixes
Write clear incident reports and recommendations
projects: Set up a small lab and collect logs from it
Write detection rules for a simulated attack
Write an incident report for a practice scenario

title: Penetration Tester
overview: Is authorised to test systems the way an attacker would, to find weaknesses before real attackers do, then explains how to fix them.
responsibilities: Plan and scope authorised tests
Probe applications, networks and configurations for weaknesses
Document findings with evidence and a fix
Retest after fixes
skills: Strong ethics and respect for scope
entryRoutes: Capture-the-flag practice on legal training platforms
Bug-bounty programmes that permit your testing
projects: Build and then attack your own vulnerable web app in a sandbox
Write up solved CTF challenges
Write a sample test report

title: Cloud Engineer
overview: Designs and operates the cloud infrastructure that applications run on, balancing reliability, security and cost.
responsibilities: Provision compute, storage and networking
Define infrastructure as code
Manage access, backups and cost
Respond to outages and capacity issues
entryRoutes: Deploy your own projects to a cloud free tier
Platform certifications, if useful to you
projects: Deploy a web app with a database using infrastructure as code
Set up a static site with a custom domain and HTTPS
Write a runbook for recovering a failed service

title: DevOps Engineer
overview: Connects development and operations by automating how software is built, tested, released and monitored.
responsibilities: Build and maintain CI/CD pipelines
Containerise and deploy services
Set up monitoring and alerting
Help teams release safely and often
entryRoutes: Automate the build and deploy of your own projects
projects: A CI pipeline that tests and deploys a small app
Containerise a multi-service app
Add a dashboard and alerts to a running service

title: Network Engineer
overview: Plans, builds and maintains the networks that connect computers, offices and data centres, and troubleshoots them when they fail.
responsibilities: Configure routers, switches and firewalls
Plan addressing and segmentation
Monitor traffic and troubleshoot faults
Document the network and changes to it
projects: Design and simulate a multi-office network
Document a home or campus network
Write a script that checks device reachability

title: UI/UX Designer
overview: Researches how people use a product and designs the screens and flows that make it clear and usable.
responsibilities: Talk to users and study how they work
Sketch flows, wireframes and prototypes
Design visual interfaces and design systems
Test designs with people and revise them
skills: A design tool such as Figma
entryRoutes: Case studies of redesigns you researched and tested
Working with a developer on a shared project
projects: Redesign one flow of an app you use, with before-and-after reasoning
Run five short usability tests and write up what you changed
Build a small design system

title: Game Developer
overview: Programs the mechanics, physics and systems of games, usually inside an engine, while balancing performance and fun.
responsibilities: Implement gameplay features
Work with artists and designers on how things look and feel
Optimise for frame rate and memory
Playtest, debug and iterate
skills: A game engine such as Unity or Unreal
entryRoutes: Finished small games and game-jam entries
projects: A complete small game in a weekend jam
A 2D platformer with your own physics
Add an enemy AI to a prototype

title: QA / SDET
overview: Makes sure software works before users find out it does not, by designing tests, writing automation and finding the cases others missed.
responsibilities: Plan test strategies and cases
Write automated tests and test tooling
Report defects with clear steps to reproduce
Work with developers to prevent repeat bugs
skills: A programming language for test automation
entryRoutes: Add automated tests to your own and open-source projects
projects: An automated test suite for a small web app
An API test harness with a readable report
A bug-hunt write-up on an app you use

title: Product Manager
overview: Decides what a team should build and why, by understanding users, the business and what is technically possible, then keeps everyone aligned.
responsibilities: Talk to users and define problems worth solving
Prioritise work and write clear requirements
Coordinate design, engineering and other teams
Use data to judge whether a feature worked
skills: Enough technical understanding to talk to engineers
entryRoutes: Lead a student project or club product
Move across from engineering, design or analytics
projects: Write a one-page product brief for an app idea, based on user interviews
Run a campus club's event process and measure the results
Prioritise a backlog for a team project and explain why
